clue.text: Defector thanks commanding officer

annotationWithheld.why: Defector thanks commanding officer (8): thanks gives TA and commanding officer CO, but no reading of the clue as held supplies TURN or puts the letters in order; probably an OCR misread or a clue cut short

clue.text: A European land bird

definitions.meaning: a country that lies partly in south-east Europe, with its capital at Ankara
a large farmyard fowl, eaten at Christmas and Thanksgiving

explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves both the nation straddling the Bosporus and the big gobbling poultry bird.

clue.text: Quite ready to accept the City way of doing things

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: fruit that is quite ready to eat is ripe
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone fully prepared to take on the financial district's methods.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; 'Quite ready' reads like an adjective phrase about a person but means fully mature.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula or method for achieving something is often called a recipe for it.

clue.text: Not in favour of a brochure constituting an agreement

parts.note: con is short for contra, against, as in pros and cons
a tract is a short pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes a leaflet that sets out the terms of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal between parties, a formal agreement.

clue.text: A president without money but with some power

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the other piece

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a US president
L stands for the pound, Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A head of state who is short of cash yet still holds some authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: ABE goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable means having the power or competence to do something.

clue.text: Run a vehicle accommodating ten possibly

indicators.note: accommodating means housing within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

indicators.note: possibly signals the word ten may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Driving a car with room for about ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb about driving but is the noun for a horse's gait; 'possibly' scrambles the number word.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's easy gait between trot and gallop is a gentle run of this kind.

clue.text: Stones a Turkish big-wig set up

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander or chief official

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word set is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gems that an Ottoman dignitary has mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' applies only to the word set, which in a down entry is read upwards beneath the Ottoman title.
explanation.definitionFit: Banded chalcedony gems are semi-precious stones.

clue.text: Having little support, the heartless leftist proceeded uncertainly

parts.note: a golf tee is a small peg supporting the ball

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a communist

explanation.surface: With scant backing, a weak left-winger stumbled along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble or sway unsteadily is to go forward hesitantly, without confidence.

clue.text: Respecting the senior nurse —-she stands out

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward

explanation.surface: A remark about a ward sister who will not give in.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds out against pressure is one who refuses to yield.

clue.text: Coin deposited in bank not long since

indicators.note: deposited in means put inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A coin was paid into a bank only a short while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb here, as in bank on: RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened lately occurred only a short time ago.

clue.text: Show affection with caution on ocean-going craft

parts.note: care is caution, as in take care
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Being tender, yet careful, aboard a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke someone gently is a way to show fondness.

clue.text: Church leader giving coppers report

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
to relate is to tell or report

explanation.surface: A bishop informs on someone to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins, pence: P.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or archbishop is a high-ranking cleric, a church leader.

clue.text: Out of drink, so send out for it

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Having run out of liquor, someone sends off for more.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods abroad for sale is to send them out of the country.

clue.text: Their beastly business is increasing

parts.note: people whose trade with animals is making them multiply: farmers raising stock

explanation.definitionFit: Stock raisers make animals multiply, so their animal trade is literally increasing numbers.

clue.text: The missile dispute

definitions.meaning: a square-headed bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crossbow bolt and a heated row between people.

clue.text: Not weighing very heavily on the conscience?

definitions.text: Not weighing very heavily on the conscience?

parts.words: Not weighing very heavily on the conscience?
parts.note: a moral qualm, and also an old apothecaries' weight of only twenty grains, so a light weight

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a twinge of moral doubt and a tiny apothecaries' weight, so a light burden on one's mind.

clue.text: Sound seed yield

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to take a word as it is spoken

parts.note: taken as written, said out loud

explanation.surface: Healthy seed produces a good harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective for healthy seed but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or hand over, as land to a conqueror, is to give way.

clue.text: Conventional view taken about mounting pictures

indicators.note: taken about means put round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: mounting means rising, so in a down clue the word art is read upwards

parts.note: art is pictures collectively

explanation.surface: A traditional opinion on how paintings should be framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' suggests framing pictures but turns ART into TRA, which SIGHT is 'taken about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone orthodox and conformist is described in slang as square or conventional.

clue.text: A sailing man in some irritation getting under way

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a smarting irritation
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor somewhat annoyed as the voyage begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning or setting off means getting going, getting under way.

clue.text: Speed of the French repair-job

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a patch is a mend or repair

explanation.surface: A French mending job done in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Despatch means promptness, haste, as in doing something with despatch.

clue.text: Glasses for youngsters

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both little drams of whisky and small children.

clue.text: Job a character found in "The Pickwick Papers"

definitions.text: Job a character found in "The Pickwick Papers"

parts.words: Job a character found in "The Pickwick Papers"
parts.note: Job is the first name of a Dickens servant, the sidekick of Alfred Jingle in that novel

explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's novel, Jingle's crafty manservant is named Job, so his surname completes the character.

clue.text: A woman writing articles about leg development

indicators.note: about means going round, so the articles surround the other piece

parts.note: an and a are the indefinite articles

indicators.note: development signals the word leg is reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A female author writing about how legs grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' turns LEG into GEL, which AN and A go 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Doctor a growth on the head that feels soft

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
hair grows on the head

explanation.surface: A physician treating a soft lump on someone's scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a verb but is the noun MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric from the Angora goat's wool is noted for its silky, soft feel.

clue.text: Saw a fellow over fifty into bed

indicators.note: into places these pieces inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: he refers to a male, a fellow
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed a man past fifty getting into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to see or observe.

clue.text: A grander ensemble might be ordered

indicators.note: the letters could be grouped together differently as a set, so the words a grander are rearranged

explanation.surface: A larger musical group may be put on order.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set out in order have been arranged.

clue.text: Work on model's face

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a model's job is to pose

explanation.surface: Doing a job on a fashion model's features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a noun, the model's face, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to confront or stand against them.

clue.text: A petition framed in simple and straightforward language

indicators.note: framed in means the letters sit inside the words simple and, held there as in a frame

explanation.surface: A request written in plain, direct words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or appeal, a petition.

clue.text: Dreadful quarters provided by Tom's employer

parts.note: grim means dreadful
E and S are compass points, two quarters

explanation.surface: Miserable lodgings offered by a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kingsley's The Water-Babies, Tom is a boy chimney sweep whose cruel master is Mr Grimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Grimes is the sweep who employs young Tom in Kingsley's novel.

clue.text: A sporting event boring some people

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
a race is a group of people of common descent

explanation.surface: A dull game for a few spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over ground without jumps is a fixture in the sporting calendar.

clue.text: Vulgar gate-keeper holding back the mob

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in reverse
holding means the words contain the letters needed, run across them

explanation.surface: A coarse doorman keeping out the rabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' points to GARGAT across vulGAR GATe, and 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tag-rag is an old word for the rabble or riff-raff.

clue.text: Grade the produce harvested

indicators.note: produce as a verb means to make something new, so the letters of grade and the are reworked

explanation.surface: Sort the crops that have been brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' reads as a noun for crops but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops brought in at harvest have been gathered.
